title: The Adarsh Housing Society Scam
dek: A 31-storey building on defence land in Mumbai was meant to house Kargil war widows and veterans. Almost none of its flats went to them — most went to bureaucrats, politicians, and their relatives.

heroStat.label: storeys built on land originally meant for war widows and veterans

promise.quote: The Adarsh Co-operative Housing Society will provide housing for widows and veterans of the 1999 Kargil war, on land allotted for that purpose.
promise.madeBy: Adarsh Co-operative Housing Society, with approvals from Maharashtra state government officials
promise.role: A housing society formed with state government cooperation, built on land with defence-adjacent status in Colaba, Mumbai
promise.context: The society was originally conceived to house Kargil war widows and army personnel, but its membership rules were repeatedly amended over the following years to admit bureaucrats, politicians, and their relatives with no connection to the military.

target.description: Flats allotted to the war widows and veterans the society was originally intended for, with construction complying with environmental and coastal-zone clearance requirements.
target.standard: The society's own founding charter and standard environmental clearance norms for coastal construction in Mumbai.

reality.description: Investigations found the society's membership had shifted almost entirely to civil servants, politicians, and their relatives, with very few Kargil-linked beneficiaries. The Bombay High Court ordered the building demolished in 2014, finding the construction illegal and its environmental clearance improperly obtained; the Supreme Court stayed that demolition in 2017 pending a CBI investigation and trial. Then-Maharashtra Chief Minister Ashok Chavan resigned over the scam in 2010.

gap.metricLabel: Storeys ordered demolished by the Bombay High Court vs. storeys actually demolished
gap.actualDisplay: 0 demolished — stayed by the Supreme Court (2017)
gap.note: The demolition order was not primarily about money but about illegal construction and fraudulent environmental clearance; this gap captures that no part of the ordered demolition has actually taken place.
